# Citing sources (APA 7)

*Example College Library research guide. © 2026 VIABLE Lab, CC BY 4.0.*

Citing tells readers where your information came from and gives credit to the people whose work you used. This guide shows APA style, 7th edition. Ask your instructor which style your class uses.

## In the text

Put the author's last name and the year in parentheses after the idea you used: (Garcia, 2021). For a direct quotation, add the page: (Garcia, 2021, p. 14). With two authors, name both (Garcia & Chen, 2021); with three or more, name the first and add "et al." (Garcia et al., 2021).

## In the reference list

The entries below show the format; the authors, works and organizations in them are made up.

List every source you cited, in alphabetical order by the first author's last name, with a hanging indent.

**Journal article**
Garcia, M., & Chen, L. (2021). Late-night phone use and sleep in adolescents. *Journal of Example Studies, 12*(3), 51–59. https://doi.org/10.0000/example

**Book**
Rivera, A. (2019). *Sleep and the teenage brain*. Example Press.

**Web page**
Example Health Council. (2022, March 1). *Teens and sleep*. https://www.example.org/teens-and-sleep

**News article**
Lee, S. (2023, September 5). Schools try later start times. *The Daily Example*. https://www.example.com/news/later-start

## Tips

- Copy the citation details when you find a source, not at the end.
- Databases often offer a "Cite" button; check its output against this guide, since it can be wrong.
- Paraphrasing still needs a citation. Only common knowledge doesn't.
